correctness.rationale: Canonical irreducible singleton/doubleton generators give exact finite profile. The exact neighboring-weight ratio and uniquely defined moving saddle center yield a uniform Gaussian envelope; logarithmic ratio expansion and dominated summation produce the displayed l1 first-order correction with \(O((m+1)^{-2})\) remainder. The embedded finite checker deduplicates independently and checks representative distributions; infinite conclusions rely on the given proof, not on sample tests.

value.rationale: A uniformly sampled finite logic-definable property with low generator rank has a natural complexity statistic, the number of singleton witnesses. The theorem resolves its scale and full phase-dependent non-Gaussian fluctuations, with a quantitative first correction valid in total variation; it distinguishes typical behavior from the maximum possible n and is not merely a restatement of known totals.
